newsitem.title: SPAIN: France Telecom makes Spain a top priority.
newsitem.headline: France Telecom makes Spain a top priority.

text.p: A top official at France Telecom said on Tuesday the group had placed a high priority on penetrating the Spanish market.

"Spain represents Europe's fifth largest telephone market with strong growth potential...it is a top priority for France Telecom," Bernard Izerable, France Telecom's senior vice president of international business in Europe told a telecoms conference in Madrid.

As part of a consortium comprising Banco Central Hispano, Deutsche Telekom and U.S. group Sprint, France Telecom has said it wants to bid for a 60 percent stake in Retevision, Spain's second basic telephone operator after Telefonica.
Retevision is due to announce on Wednesday its decision on which groups may bid.
On a global basis, France Telecom said it intended to expand its Global One partnership with Deutsche Telekom and Sprint, and pursue local partners in local markets.
"We want to expand Global One as a full service carrier and we want to expand our operations in emerging markets...but we need a domestic presence in major world markets," Izerable said.
On the Spanish market, France Telecom said it would offer, through its consortium, a full range of telephone services including long distance and the local loop.
The number one priority will be customer focus followed by competitive pricing, he said.
Among conditions vital for success in the Spanish market, Izerable cited full competition, a clear regulatory framework, and the the right services at the right price.

Industry sources expect that three different groups will be allowed to bid for the government's 60 percent stake in Retevision: the France Telecom consortium; Mannesmann and AT&T ; and a group including Stet International, Endesa, Union Fenosa and Basque group Euskatel.
